findings.source_quote: Μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν, φασί, κοιμηθήσῃ ὡς ἀδελφός, καὶ οὐχ ὡς ἀνήρ.
findings.english_quote: Retain the narrated affection, sibling distinction, the Son’s role and the stated gate/name and clothing requirements.
findings.issue: The unit-level theological metadata attributes the Son’s role and gate/name and clothing requirements to this section. Those assertions are not present in the selected source. The linen tunics in paragraph 7 are bedding, not a stated clothing requirement. This appears to be metadata carried over from other sections.
findings.suggested_revision: Restrict this unit’s decision to its actual contents: the narrated affection, brother/not-husband distinction, overnight stay, prayer, and supper metaphor. If the other claims describe a multi-section decision, label that scope explicitly and identify the relevant units rather than presenting them as contents of xi.

findings.source_quote: Σήμερον ὁ ποιμὴν ὧδε οὐκ ἔρχεται.
findings.english_quote: The shepherd will not come today.
findings.issue: Omitting “here” broadens the negated assertion. The source says that the shepherd is not coming to this location today, not that he will make no arrival anywhere.
findings.suggested_revision: “The shepherd will not come here today.”

findings.source_quote: κἀγὼ ὡσεὶ νεώτερος ἐγεγόνειν καὶ ἠρξάμην καὶ αὐτὸς παίζειν μετ᾿ αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: I felt younger and began playing with them.
findings.issue: The simplified text drops the explicit “as though” comparison. The source describes his experience as if he had become younger; it does not simply assert that he felt younger. The standard edition preserves this qualification.
findings.suggested_revision: “I felt as if I had become younger, and I too began playing with them.”

findings.source_quote: Καθὼς, φημί, κύριε, ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς ἔδειξας, ἐρωτῶ σε, κύριε, ἵνα καθὼς ἄν σε ἐπερωτήσω, οὕτω μοι καὶ δηλώσῃς.
findings.english_quote: Sir, explain what you showed me from the beginning as I ask you about it.
findings.issue: The opening comparison, “just as you showed … from the beginning,” has been recast as the object of “explain”: “what you showed me.” This loses the source’s comparison between the earlier showing and the requested question-by-question explanation. It also removes the explicit framing as a request.
findings.suggested_revision: A candidate for fresh review is: “Sir, just as you showed me things from the beginning, I ask you to explain them to me as I ask you questions.” Preserve the comparison and request without claiming that this is the only possible interpretation.

findings.source_quote: Μεθ᾿ ἡμῶν, φασί, κοιμηθήσῃ ὡς ἀδελφός, καὶ οὐχ ὡς ἀνήρ.
findings.english_quote: Retain the narrated affection, sibling distinction, the Son’s role and the stated gate/name and clothing requirements.
findings.issue: The theological metadata attributes requirements and a statement about the Son to this unit that are absent from the selected source. The tunics used as bedding do not constitute a clothing requirement.
findings.suggested_revision: Replace this with a decision scoped to xi’s affection, sibling distinction, overnight stay, prayer, and supper metaphor, or explicitly identify it as a multi-section decision with references to the other units.

findings.source_quote: ἔστρωσαν γὰρ αἱ παρθένοι τοὺς λινοῦς χιτῶνας ἑαυτῶν χαμαί
findings.english_quote: Retain ancient repair materials, sibling relationship and affection, gate/name requirements, holy-spirits plural and clothing imagery; preserve all substantive alternative notes.
findings.issue: The simplification metadata claims preservation of ancient repair materials, gate/name requirements, and a holy-spirits plural, none of which occurs in xi. It therefore does not accurately document this edition’s simplification decisions.
findings.suggested_revision: Document the actual simplifications in this unit and the distinctions they preserve, including the tunics as bedding, prayer, the second hour, the affectionate actions, and the brother/not-husband contrast. Remove unrelated claims or explicitly relocate them to their proper units.

summary: Both editions require revision. The standard text substantially covers the selected Greek, but its unit-level metadata includes claims from other sections. Independent review of the simplified text also identifies a broadened negation, a lost comparison, and a changed request structure. The disclosed working readings and bracketed dance phrase need not be replaced merely because alternatives exist. The apparatus notes are treated as attributed edition reports, not fresh manuscript verification; this review does not authenticate unseen editions or certify an exhaustive collation. All proposed replacements require fresh review.
